problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Find the values of $a$ and $b$, if 

$$
{f}_{x}(x,y)=y(1+x){e}^{x}+ax{y}^{3}+3{x}^{2},\,{f}_{y}(x,y)=bx{e}^{x}-3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Find the values of $a$ and $b$, if 

$$
{f}_{x}(x,y)=a{x}^{2}y-4{y}^{2}+3,\,{f}_{y}(x,y)=2{x}^{3}+bxy-8.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the mixed partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(a{x}^{2}y-4{y}^{2}+3) \\  & =a{x}^{2}-8y \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{3}+bxy-8) \\  & =6{x}^{2}+by\end{aligned}
$$

Since the function and its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. Hence, we have the identity

$$
\begin{aligned}a{x}^{2}-8y=6{x}^{2}+by.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of ${x}^{2}$ and $y,$ respectively, we see that $a=6$ and $b=-8.$
